exposure: Early universal ultrasound (US) screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH)
Risk factors (female gender, breech presentation, positive family history)
outcome: Effectiveness of early universal US screening (detection of DDH)
Sensitivity and specificity of clinical examinations
cohort: The study included 1636 mature neonates (3272 hips) who underwent clinical examinations and hip ultrasound within the first 3 days of life.
finding: Early universal ultrasound screening was found to be highly effective in detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip, diagnosing all cases, even in 50.9% of newborns who lacked positive physical signs or risk factors other than being female, while clinical examination had low sensitivity (20%).
mod_finding: Breech presentation was identified as a significant risk factor for developmental dysplasia of the hip.
